verdict.rationale: Logseq's own docs make storage location a per-graph choice: a graph can stay local-only or be synced through Logseq Sync. Community users confirm the data is local, so users control residency by keeping data on their own device. There is no evidence of choosing a region or residency for synced or cloud-hosted data. Third-party routes such as Syncthing or iCloud are user workarounds and earn no credit. Missing for 10: selectable region/residency for Logseq Sync storage, documentation of where sync servers are located, independent corroboration of residency controls.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Syncing is a choice that is made per graph and thus allows for some graphs to be local only.
no mandatory subscription, local data, and source availability
